title: High-Value Lapsed App Users — Win-Back Segmentation
summary: Segment a synthetic customer base into high-value, lapsed, app-installed, email-disengaged customers; apply support suppression, channel opt-ins, PII removal, and overlap analysis against six existing audiences.
taskPrompt:
You are a digital marketing analyst building a re-engagement audience from customer
profiles.

## Task Directory

`base`

## Your Task

1. Read `base/input/segmentation_brief.md`, `base/input/governance_policies.yaml`, and
   `base/input/data_dictionary.tsv`.
2. Load `base/input/unified_profiles.csv`.
3. Identify customers matching every target condition in the brief.
4. Suppress customers with active support tickets, then compute SMS and push eligibility.
5. Remove `age`, `gender`, `city`, and `state` from the output roster.
6. Compute overlap against each audience in `base/input/existing_audiences.csv`.
7. Write exactly the three contracted output files under `base/output`.

## Required Outputs

- `base/output/segment_definition.json`
- `base/output/audience_roster.csv`
- `base/output/overlap_report.tsv`

The exact schemas, target conditions, channel rules, PII rules, overlap formula, and required
constant values are in `base/input/segmentation_brief.md`. Follow them exactly.

## Environment

Python 3.12 is available. The standard library is sufficient; pandas and pyarrow are optional.
agentMustDo: Read the segmentation brief, governance policies, and data dictionary.
Filter unified_profiles.csv to the target conditions; suppress active support tickets.
Compute SMS, push, and any-channel eligibility after suppression.
Remove age, gender, city, and state from the roster.
Compute overlaps against all six existing audiences using overlap_count / total_qualifying * 100.
Write segment_definition.json, audience_roster.csv, and overlap_report.tsv exactly as contracted.

inputFiles.name: segmentation_brief.md
inputFiles.description: Target conditions, governance, and output contract.

inputFiles.name: governance_policies.yaml
inputFiles.description: PII, opt-in, minimum-size, and suppression policies.

inputFiles.name: data_dictionary.tsv
inputFiles.description: Field names, types, and permitted values.

referenceFiles.name: segment_definition.json
referenceFiles.description: Segment predicates, suppression, channels, governance, and stats.

referenceFiles.name: audience_roster.csv
referenceFiles.description: Qualifying roster with PII removed and eligibility flags.

referenceFiles.name: overlap_report.tsv
referenceFiles.description: Overlap counts and percentages against six audiences.

evaluation: Hard gates: missing or unparsable outputs, PII columns in the roster, audience below the governance minimum, wrong target set, wrong eligibility flags, wrong stats, or wrong overlap counts/percentages. The score is the fraction of checks passed; only a fully correct submission scores 1.0.

classifier.rationale: The task performs marketing audience segmentation with governance and overlap analysis.
